original_value: Research findings have shown that microphones can be uniquely identified by audio recordings since physical features of the microphone components leave repeatable and distinguishable traces on the audio stream. This property can be exploited in security applications to perform the identification of a mobile phone through the built-in microphone. The problem is to determine an accurate but also efficient representation of the physical characteristics, which is not known a priori. Usually there is a trade-off between the identification accuracy and the time requested to perform the classification. Various approaches have been used in literature to deal with it, ranging from the application of handcrafted statistical features to the recent application of deep learning techniques. This paper evaluates the application of different entropy measures (Shannon Entropy, Permutation Entropy, Dispersion Entropy, Approximate Entropy, Sample Entropy, and Fuzzy Entropy) and their suitability for microphone classification. The analysis is validated against an experimental dataset of built-in microphones of 34 mobile phones, stimulated by three different audio signals. The findings show that selected entropy measures can provide a very high identification accuracy in comparison to other statistical features and that they can be robust against the presence of noise. This paper performs an extensive analysis based on filter features selection methods to identify the most discriminating entropy measures and the related hyper-parameters (e.g., embedding dimension). Results on the trade-off between accuracy and classification time are also presented.

result.paraphrase: Research has shown that microphones can be uniquely recognized from audio recordings because the physical characteristics of their components leave consistent, distinctive traces in the audio stream. This can be leveraged in security applications to identify a mobile phone through its built-in microphone. The challenge is to find an accurate yet efficient representation of these physical characteristics, which is not known in advance. Typically, there is a trade-off between identification accuracy and the time required for classification. To address this, prior work has explored approaches ranging from handcrafted statistical features to recent deep learning techniques. This paper examines the use of several entropy measures—Shannon Entropy, Permutation Entropy, Dispersion Entropy, Approximate Entropy, Sample Entropy, and Fuzzy Entropy—and assesses their suitability for microphone classification. The analysis is validated on an experimental dataset of built-in microphones from 34 mobile phones, tested with three different audio signals. The results indicate that selected entropy measures can achieve very high identification accuracy compared with other statistical features and can remain robust in the presence of noise. The paper also presents an extensive analysis using filter feature selection methods to determine the most discriminative entropy measures and the associated hyper-parameters, such as embedding dimension. Results on the balance between accuracy and classification time are likewise reported.
